reading: The left column stays; a diagonal of 2 runs from the top-right corner down to just above the bottom-left, and the bottom row (except column 0) becomes 4.

new_rows.name: antidiag
new_rows.datalog:
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
antidiag(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), w(W), h(H), X2 = W - Y, X = X2, Y < H.

new_rows.name: base_row
new_rows.datalog:
h(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
base_row(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), h(H), Y = H, X > 0.

why: cells with X+Y = W-1 above the last row are 2; the last row from column 1 on is 4; everything else is unchanged

reading: Among the 0-shapes (a block with a 2-cell bump), the one level with the colour-5 staircase loses its bump, and the body column on the side facing the staircase turns 6.

slots.subject: the 0-shape whose rows overlap the 5 staircase
slots.marked: the body's edge column facing the 5 staircase, recoloured 6

why: exactly one 0-shape changes; its bump cells become background and one full edge line of its body becomes 6

reading: Four same-colour corner cells mark a box; the output is the inside of that box, with the shape recoloured to the corner colour.

new_rows.name: inner
new_rows.datalog:
y0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
y1(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x1(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inner(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), y0(A), y1(B), x0(L), x1(R), Y > A, Y < B, X > L, X < R.

new_rows.name: inner_fg
new_rows.datalog:
y0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
y1(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x1(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inner_fg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), y0(A), y1(B), x0(L), x1(R), Y > A, Y < B, X > L, X < R.

why: the corner cells sit at the four corners of the foreground box; output = that box minus its border rows/columns, every shape cell in the corner colour

reading: Each single 3 gets a fixed 5x5 house around it (5 roof, 2 walls, 5 above the 3, 8 floor), and the floor row is extended across the whole grid in 2.

new_rows.name: ground
new_rows.datalog:
nb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C2).
mk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !nb(Y, X).
ground(Y2, X) :- mk(Y, X0), Y2 = Y + 2, px(Y2, X, C).

why: the full row two below each 3 is 2 except where the 5x5 unit centred on the 3 overwrites it; unit rows: 55555 / 2.5.2 / 2.3.2 / 2...2 / 88888

reading: Two vertical 5 bars capped by 8s frame a box; the output is that box (5 bars plus the 8 caps) cut out, discarding the scattered 8 noise outside.

new_rows.name: box5
new_rows.datalog:
t5(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, 5).
b5(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, 5).
l5(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, 5).
r5(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, 5).
box5(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), t5(T), b5(B), l5(L), r5(R), T1 = T - 1, B1 = B + 1, Y >= T1, Y <= B1, X >= L, X <= R.

why: output = input cut to the box of the 5 cells widened by one row above and below

reading: Scattered dots slide straight toward the 5 band until they touch it (stacking on each other) and turn 5.

new_rows.name: dots
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(max(N)) :- osize(O, N).
band(O) :- osize(O, N), big(N).
dots(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), !band(O).

why: per row (vertical band) or column (horizontal band), the k dots on one side become k cells of 5 stacked against the band on that side
invariants: dot counts per line and side

reading: Every single 5 gets a 3x3 ring of 1 around it.
why: each 5 is the centre of an identical 3x3 unit (1 border, 5 centre); other cells unchanged

reading: The grid holds 5x5 outlined boxes; each box with an empty inside copies the 3x3 inner pattern of another box of the same colour that has one.

slots.units: the 5x5 outline boxes in the 6-cell lattice
slots.source: a box of colour c whose 3x3 interior is non-empty
slots.target: every box of colour c with an empty interior
slots.action: paste the source interior into the target interior

why: each colour has at most one distinct interior pattern; empty boxes of a colour with no patterned twin stay empty

reading: Each 1 cup with a gap on top holds one coloured dot; the cup's inside, the gap, and the row just above the cup are filled with the dot's colour.

new_rows.name: cupfill
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
cup(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 1.
ct(O, min(Y)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
cb(O, max(Y)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
cl(O, min(X)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
cr(O, max(X)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
cupfill(Y, X) :- ct(O, T), cb(O, B), cl(O, L), cr(O, R), px(Y, X, C), C = 0, T1 = T - 1, Y >= T1, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R.

why: every background cell in each cup's box extended one row up takes the colour of the dot inside that cup

reading: A dashed 1 rectangle (sometimes with one dashed inner line) is completed: gaps along the dashed lines are filled with 2.

new_rows.name: dash_gaps
new_rows.datalog:
rowc(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
colc(X, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
y0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
y1(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
x1(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
dash_gaps(Y, X) :- rowc(Y, N), N >= 4, px(Y, X, C), C = 0, x0(A), x1(B), X >= A, X <= B.
dash_gaps(Y, X) :- colc(X, N), N >= 4, px(Y, X, C), C = 0, y0(A), y1(B), Y >= A, Y <= B.

why: a row or column with at least 4 cells of 1 is a dashed line; its background cells within the 1-box become 2; nothing else changes
